title.narrative: Joint Devolution Programme for Improved Public Service Delivery

description.narrative: The Joint Devolution Programme (JDP) is a partnership between UNDP, UNICEF, and UN Women with the Government of Kenya to strengthen decentralized service delivery, inclusive governance, and gender equality in line with Kenya’s Constitution, Vision 2030, BETA priorities, and the UNSDCF (2022–2026). Building on lessons from earlier devolution programmes, the JDP was designed through extensive consultations with national and county governments, oversight institutions, civil society, private sector, and marginalized groups, ensuring a strong participatory foundation. It seeks to consolidate devolution gains—such as improved service delivery and civic engagement—while addressing persistent gaps in public participation quality, social accountability, gender-responsive and climate-sensitive planning, and budget oversight. The programme is structured around three interlinked outputs: (i) strengthening inclusive public participation and oversight, (ii) improving county planning and budgeting frameworks that integrate SDG localization, climate resilience, and intergovernmental coordination, and (iii) promoting evidence-based, data-driven knowledge management for policy and decision-making. With a Programme Management Unit embedded in the State Department for Devolution and the Council of Governors guiding coordination, the JDP will leverage the comparative advantages of the UN agencies to catalyze scalable reforms, empower local communities, promote sustainable development and resilience, and advance SDGs 5, 10, 11, 16, and 17.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
